Thanks for the heads up. I'm pulling the serving traces now. Initial observations from infra: model-B introduces a slightly larger KV cache footprint and a new attention kernel variant that regresses on long-prefetch sequences (seen most when clients send prefix prompts > 1k tokens).

Preliminary mitigation options I want to propose (quick list):
1) Pause the model-B rollout for FastRetail cohort (immediate, quick revert)
2) Force model routing to the previous baseline model variant for impacted routes while we analyze traces
3) Apply a temporary per-tenant max-seq-length to keep kernels in the optimized path (short-term)

I'll attach the initial trace snippets from the serving cluster in the next message. If you authorize, I can pause the cohort now.

-Marcus
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

Sanjay — quick update and apology for the latency window. Marcus performed a manual pause of the model-B profile for the FastRetail cohort at 10:05 PT on 2026-05-01, which returned routing to the baseline model variant. After the rollback we observed p95 drop back to ~240ms and p99 back under 600ms in our Canary metrics within 18 minutes.

Root cause (preliminary): a kernel-path regression for the new attention variant under long prefix sequences which increased KV cache pressure and caused higher queueing on some GPU pools. Marcus will lead a more detailed postmortem with timeline and mitigation commitments.

Next steps we will execute and share by EOD:
- Marcus to provide kernel traces and patch timeline (ENG-3245)
- CS to share customer-facing incident summary and any credits (MON-INC-987)
- Product to update rollout gating for model profiles to include a longer long-tail perf probe and tenant-specific preflight checks

We sincerely apologize for the disruption. Monica and I will coordinate the postmortem and any commercial remedies. I'll follow up with the formal incident summary and meeting invite.
